newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bank VUB SKK 1.5 bln, 2-yr bond issue Dec 9.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bank VUB SKK 1.5 bln, 2-yr bond issue Dec 9.

text.p: Slovak bank VUB a.s. will issue a 1.5 billion crown tranche of two-year bonds on December 9, the bank said in a published statement on Friday.
The issue will carry a fixed annual coupon of 12.25 percent, some 50 basis points over the IFC's three-year Slovak crown-denominated bond issue of last July.
No further details were disclosed. Bank officials were not immediately available for comment.
In February 1996, VUB issued a 1.0 billion crown tranche of three-year bond, with fixed interest of 11.7 percent.
This was followed by a 1.5 billion crown tranche of five-year bond in June, with a coupon rate of 10.75 percent.
VUB is Slovakia's largest commercial bank and accounts for about 60 percent of company loans in the country.

The bank was partialy-privatised in the first wave of voucher privatisation launched in 1992. It is still controlled by the state through a 47.8 percent stake held by the privatisation agency, the National Property Fund.
Investment funds and other banks hold 40.72 percent in VUB, with the remainder shared by small shareholders and the state restitution fund.
VUB is one of the four major Slovak financial institutions awaiting full privatisation. The programme, however, had been postponed until March 31, 1997.
